quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No turns allowed.
No outlet ahead.
No U-turns allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that U-turns are not allowed. You will often see this sign at intersections with heavy oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What can you drive with a Class C driver license?

options.text: Any motor vehicle, no matter how large or heavy.
A vehicle weighing less than 26,001 pounds.
A vehicle weighing more than 26,001 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle weighing less than 26,001 pounds.
questions.explanation: A Class C license allows you to drive any vehicle that weighs less than 26,001 pounds.

questions.question: You see a green light, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partly enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Wait until you can drive all the way through the intersection before entering.
Drive into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can drive all the way through the intersection before entering.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter the intersection unless you can drive all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Frequently to see traffic moving behind you.
Only to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently to see traffic moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Do not stare straight ahead while driving. Check your rearview mirrors often so you always know where nearby vehicles are.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. How can you prevent it in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Reduce your speed.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down when the pavement is wet to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A 35 mph speed zone begins after the curve.
Drive at least 35 mph around the upcoming curve.
Go 35 mph or slower when you reach the upcoming curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go 35 mph or slower when you reach the upcoming curve.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black text. They tell you about conditions just ahead. Speed advisory signs under them show the safe speed for that area.

questions.question: As your blood alcohol level (BAC) increases, what happens to you?

options.text: You become more intoxicated.
You become more sober.
You become more coordinated.

questions.correctAnswerText: You become more intoxicated.
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: What headlights should you use in rain or fog to see better?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you, even if they don't help you see much better.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Look in your inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Look in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all areas around your vehicle. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to see areas that mirrors cannot show.

questions.question: When is turning or stopping most dangerous in rainy weather?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after the rain stops.
During the first 30 minutes of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 30 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when turning and stopping in the first 30 minutes of rain. During this time, oil from vehicles has not yet washed off the road and creates a slippery surface with the rain.

questions.question: When you are preparing to turn left from a two-way street, where should you position your car?

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the centerline.
On the left side of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, start in the lane closest to the centerline. Begin your turn just before your car reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn smoothly into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can you have before your driving is affected?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: When is the traditional mirror setting appropriate?

options.text: It may be useful for large vehicles when towing or backing in tight spaces.
It does not show the edge of the vehicle.
It is appropriate for all vehicles in all situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may be useful for large vehicles when towing or backing in tight spaces.
questions.explanation: After adjusting your seat properly, adjust your left mirror to see the left edge of your vehicle and your right mirror to see the right edge. This traditional mirror setting is most useful for drivers of trucks, vans, and SUVs when towing or backing in tight spaces.

questions.question: When bicycles are used on roadways, what are they considered?

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are considered vehicles when used on roadways. Bicyclists and drivers must follow the same rules of the road.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road will curve right first, then curve left. Slow down to safely navigate the curves ahead.

questions.question: What problems can a bad suspension cause?

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and gives you a comfortable ride. If your vehicle bounces a lot after hitting a bump or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: The driver ahead stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Carefully pass at 10 mph or slower.
Stop and go only when all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and go only when all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. There may be pedestrians you cannot see. Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have crossed.

questions.question: Before you change lanes, you should check your mirrors and also:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your current lane.
Look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, you must look behind you. Turn and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicle is in your blind spot. Also check that no other driver is moving into the same lane from another direction.

questions.question: When driving in heavy fog, what should you do?

options.text: Use your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If the fog is too thick and you cannot see, pull off the road safely and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: Which statement about pedal control is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake hard to make sure you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply brakes gently with steady pressure so your vehicle stops smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Expect the child to have full control of the bicycle.
Be ready for anything.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable. Young riders often make sudden changes in direction. Bicycles and children are small and hard to see, so always be prepared for sudden moves.

questions.question: When driving at night, what should you do?

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming cars.
Stay farther behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: When it is dark and hard to see, increase the distance between your car and the one ahead. Use your headlights properly. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights because the brightness can blind you.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving at the same speed.
questions.explanation: When another car is passing you, do not speed up or brake. Keep your speed steady and let the other vehicle pass safely and return to your lane.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal fast several times.
Slow down slowly and avoid braking hard.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down slowly and avoid braking hard.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car going straight. Let off the gas and do not brake hard. Let the car slow down on its own. Use light braking only if you need to. Once you are safe, pull off the road.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street. Why?

options.text: To spot problems before they happen.
Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your car completely.
To keep up with traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot problems before they happen.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for traffic changes ahead. Look for signals from other drivers. Be ready for cars entering at on-ramps and expect sudden changes in road and traffic conditions.
